The 2018–19 season was [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s 27th season in the [[Premier League]] and their 44th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. The season was the first since 2005–06 without club captain [[Michael Carrick]], who retired after the [[2017–18 Manchester United F.C. season|2017–18 season]] and joined the club's coaching staff.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Carrick confirms summer retirement |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2018/Mar/michael-carrick-confirms-retirement-from-playing-career-at-end-of-the-season.aspx |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=12 March 2018 |access-date=3 April 2018 }}</ref> Assistant manager [[Rui Faria]] left the club at the conclusion of that season, with Carrick and [[Kieran McKenna]] replacing him as the club's first-team coaches.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Jamie |last=Jackson |title=Manchester United assistant manager Rui Faria to leave Old Trafford |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/may/12/manchester-united-assistant-manager-rui-faria-to-leave-club |website=The Guardian |date=12 May 2018 |access-date=15 July 2018 }}</ref>

A disappointing [[2018–19 Premier League|Premier League]] campaign saw the club finish in sixth place. United were also eliminated early in the [[2018–19 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], losing on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] to [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] in the third round. The club reached the quarter-final stage of both the [[2018–19 FA Cup|FA Cup]] and the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], but were eliminated by [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] respectively. This resulted in United's first consecutive trophyless seasons in [[1988–89 Manchester United F.C. season|30 years]]. On 5 May 2019, following a draw at bottom-placed [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]], United confirmed their place in the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League]], making it the fourth time they had finished outside of the top four in the league since 2014.

On 18 December 2018, with just seven wins in the first 17 league games, manager [[José Mourinho]] was sacked. His last game, two days earlier, ended in a [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|3–1 defeat]] to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Jose Mourinho: Manchester United sack manager |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46603018 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 December 2018 |access-date=18 December 2018 }}</ref> The following day, former United striker [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] was appointed as [[caretaker manager]] until the end of the season, assisted by former coach [[Mike Phelan]], who had left the club in 2013 following the retirement of Sir Alex Ferguson.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ole Gunnar Solskjaer appointed caretaker manager |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/ole-gunnar-solskjaer-appointed-caretaker-manager |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=19 December 2018 |access-date=19 December 2018 }}</ref> On 28 March 2019, Solskjær became full-time manager.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/manchester-united-announces-ole-gunnar-solskjaer-as-full-time-manager|title=Manchester United announces Ole Gunnar Solskjaer as full time manager|website=ManUtd.com|date=28 March 2019|publisher=Manchester United |access-date=28 March 2019}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
{{see also|2018 International Champions Cup}}
United preceded their 2018–19 campaign with a tour of the United States. The first three games were announced on 3 April 2018, with the opposition provided by [[Club América]], [[San Jose Earthquakes]] and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite news |title=United to return to US for Tour 2018 |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Tour-2018/Tour-2018-News/2018/Mar/manchester-united-confirm-return-to-usa-for-pre-season-tour-2018.aspx |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |access-date=3 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180404211127/http://www.manutd.com/en/Tour-2018/Tour-2018-News/2018/Mar/manchester-united-confirm-return-to-usa-for-pre-season-tour-2018.aspx |archive-date=4 April 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The club later announced that the tour would see them compete in the International Champions Cup.<ref>{{cite news |first=Gemma |last=Thompson |title=United to take part in ICC |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Tour-2018/Tour-2018-News/2018/Apr/tour-2018-manchester-united-to-take-part-international-champions-cup-in-usa.aspx |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=10 April 2018 |access-date=10 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180415064649/http://www.manutd.com/en/Tour-2018/Tour-2018-News/2018/Apr/tour-2018-manchester-united-to-take-part-international-champions-cup-in-usa.aspx |archive-date=15 April 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the 2018 competition, United played against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] at the [[StubHub Center]] in [[Carson, California]], Liverpool at the [[Michigan Stadium]] in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], and [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] at the [[Hard Rock Stadium]] in [[Miami Gardens, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tournament Schedule |url=https://www.internationalchampionscup.com/en/men/matches/schedule |publisher=International Champions Cup |access-date=8 June 2018 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612150409/https://www.internationalchampionscup.com/en/men/matches/schedule |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Alexis Sánchez]]'s arrival in the United States was delayed as he was not issued with a [[Visa policy of the United States|visa]] due to the 16-month suspended jail sentence he accepted in February for [[Tax evasion|tax fraud]] during his time in Spain.<ref>{{cite news |title=Alexis Sanchez: Man Utd striker misses start of US tour because of visa issue |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44850992 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 July 2018 |access-date=17 July 2018 }}</ref> The final pre-season game saw Manchester United play away to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] at the [[Allianz Arena]] on 5 August.<ref>{{cite news |title=United to face Bayern Munich in pre-season |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/manchester-united-announces-pre-season-friendly-with-bayern-munich |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=11 June 2018 |access-date=11 June 2018 }}</ref>

==FA Cup==
{{main article|2018–19 FA Cup}}
As one of the 20 teams in the Premier League, Manchester United entered the FA Cup in the Third Round. The draw was made on 3 December 2018 and paired United with [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], whom they had faced at the same stage [[2016–17 FA Cup|two seasons earlier]], when they won 4–0.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Froggatt |title=United to face Reading in FA Cup Third Round |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/details-of-fa-cup-third-round-draw-for-man-united |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=3 December 2018 |access-date=3 December 2018 }}</ref> United won the match 2–0; [[Juan Mata]] opened the scoring from the [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty spot]] after the [[video assistant referee]] ruled that [[Omar Richards]] had tripped [[Juan Mata]] in the penalty area, and another goal from [[Romelu Lukaku]]. 19-year-old winger [[Tahith Chong]] made his FA Cup debut, replacing [[Juan Mata]] in the 62nd minute.<ref>{{Cite news |first1=Chris |last1=Knight |first2=Tom |last2=Marshall-Bailey |title=VAR awards United a penalty after Juan Mata is fouled in the penalty area |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/var-in-fa-cup-mata-15634133 |website=Manchester Evening News |publisher=MEN Media |date=5 January 2019 |access-date=5 January 2019 }}</ref> The draw for the Fourth Round was made on 7 January 2019 and United were drawn away to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]];<ref>{{Cite news |title=FA Cup fourth-round draw: Arsenal host Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46777424 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 January 2019 |access-date=5 January 2019 }}</ref> the last time the two sides had met in the FA Cup was in the Sixth Round of the 2014–15 season, when Arsenal won 2–1 at Old Trafford.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Manchester United 1-2 Arsenal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31689011 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 March 2015 |access-date=31 January 2019 }}</ref> This time Manchester United won 3–1; two goals in two minutes from former Arsenal forward [[Alexis Sánchez]] and [[Jesse Lingard]] put United 2–0 up with just over half an hour played, but [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] got one back for the Gunners shortly before half-time. [[Anthony Martial]] then came off the bench to seal the win for United with their third goal in the 82nd minute.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Arsenal 1-3 Manchester United in FA Cup fourth round |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46914273 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 January 2019 |access-date=31 January 2019 }}</ref> The draw for the Fifth Round was made on 28 January 2019 and United were drawn away to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], whom they had faced in the final the previous season.<ref>{{Cite news |title=FA Cup: Holders Chelsea draw Man Utd in FA Cup fifth round |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47021610 |date=28 January 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=29 January 2019 }}</ref> Goals from [[Paul Pogba]] and [[Ander Herrera]] before half-time sealed a 2–0 win for United.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=FA Cup: Man Utd knock Chelsea out of FA Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47194019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 February 2019 |access-date=19 February 2019 }}</ref> They were then drawn away to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] in the quarter-finals. Goals from [[Raúl Jiménez]] and [[Diogo Jota]] gave Wolves a 2–1 win and a place in the semi-finals, with [[Marcus Rashford]] scoring a consolation goal for United in the 95th minute.<ref>{{Cite news |title=FA Cup quarter-final draw: Man Utd face Wolves in last eight |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47283939 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 February 2019 |access-date=19 February 2019 }}</ref>

==EFL Cup==
{{main article|2018–19 EFL Cup}}
The draw for the third round of the EFL Cup was made on 30 August 2018, with Manchester United drawn at home to [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Carabao Cup Round Three Draw Confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2018/august/carabao-cup-round-three-draw2/ |publisher=[[English Football League]] |date=30 August 2018 |access-date=30 August 2018}}</ref> United took the lead just three minutes in through Juan Mata, but an equaliser from Harry Wilson was followed by a red card for United keeper Romero. Marriot gave Derby the lead with five minutes to go, but Marouane Fellaini's stoppage-time strike ensured penalties; however Derby won 8-7 on spot kicks.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45555895|title = Derby beat Man Utd 8-7 in shootout|work = BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Knockout phase===
{{main|2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}
The draw for the round of 16 was held on 17 December 2018, 12:00 [[Central European Time|CET]], at the UEFA headquarters in [[Nyon]], Switzerland.<ref name="r16draw">{{cite news |title=UEFA Champions League round of 16 draw confirmed |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/024c-0e994e4aa0a2-2e25ae292aec-1000--uefa-champions-league-round-of-16-draw-confirmed/ |access-date=17 December 2018 |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=17 December 2018 }}</ref> After finishing second in their group and progressing to the round of 16, United were drawn against French champions [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the first competitive meeting between the two sides.<ref name="r16draw"/> In the first leg at Old Trafford, goals from [[Presnel Kimpembe]] and [[Kylian Mbappé]] gave PSG a 2–0 lead to take back to the [[Parc des Princes]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47190655|title=Man Utd 0-2 PSG: Kimpembe and Mbappe earn win for PSG|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 February 2019|access-date=7 March 2019}}</ref> Needing to score three times to progress, Romelu Lukaku opened the scoring for United in the second minute of the second leg, before [[Juan Bernat]] restored PSG's two-goal aggregate lead less than 10 minutes later. Lukaku then scored again after half an hour, to bring United within a goal of the quarter-finals. Former Manchester United midfielder [[Ángel Di María]] had the ball in the back of the net early in the second half, only for the goal to be ruled out for offside, and Bernat hit the post late on after Mbappé had rounded David de Gea. In the 90th minute, referee [[Damir Skomina]] awarded United a penalty after using a [[video assistant referee|VAR]] review to adjudge Kimpembe to have handled the ball in the penalty area. Marcus Rashford scored the spot-kick to make it 3–3 on aggregate and send United through to the quarter-finals on the [[away goals rule]]; this made them the first team in Champions League history to progress after losing by at least two goals at home in the first leg.<ref name="BBC">{{Cite news|first=Shamoon|last=Hafez|title=Champions League: PSG 1-3 Man Utd (agg: 3-3) |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47461886|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 March 2019|access-date=7 March 2019}}</ref> Solskjær gave 17-year-old forward [[Mason Greenwood]] and 19-year-old winger [[Tahith Chong]] their European debuts, the former also playing his first senior game.<ref name="BBC"/>

The draw for the quarter-finals was held on 15 March 2019,<ref name="QF_draw">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/draws/2019/2000982/ |title=UEFA Champions League quarter-final draw |website=[[UEFA]] |access-date=10 March 2019}}</ref> with United paired with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]. Both United and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] were originally drawn to play their home legs in the same week; as United finished lower in the league the [[2017–18 Premier League|previous season]], their tie was reversed. The first leg was played at Old Trafford on 10 April 2019. Barcelona won 1–0 thanks to an own goal by [[Luke Shaw]] that was originally ruled out for offside; the decision was later overturned after a [[video assistant referee|VAR]] review. The second leg was played at [[Camp Nou]] on 16 April, with two goals from [[Lionel Messi]] and another from former Liverpool forward [[Philippe Coutinho]] giving the Spanish side a 3–0 win on the night, 4–0 on aggregate.
